note: Edward Hopper's life, kept to what a named source states. Every entry carries the source that says it and a link to that page; nothing here is written from memory, and where two sources disagree the entry says so rather than choosing quietly. This is a reminder for somebody reading a dated ledger leaf — not a biography, and not a substitute for one. From 2026 the black notebook of Josephine Hopper, transcribed on this site, is one of the sources: what it states is quoted in her words and linked to the page she wrote it on, and the pictures and journeys in it are as often hers as his. From September 2026 two of the five parts of Madeleine Larson's typed transcripts at PAAM are sources too — all five parts, read page by page off the scans, since they carry no text layer — 389 typescript pages. Each event names the part and the typescript's own page number.

events.what: The house in Nyack that his maternal grandparents built — Hopper’s home until 1910.
Born in Nyack, New York, thirty miles up the Hudson from Manhattan.
Begins commuting into the city to study at the New York School of Illustrating.
Enrols at the New York School of Art; studies under William Merritt Chase, and prefers the classes of Robert Henri and Kenneth Hayes Miller.
Begins supporting himself as a commercial artist and illustrator — work he will go on doing for about twenty years. The first three decades of Book IV are its record.
First of three extended stays in Paris, the last of them in 1910; he begins painting out of doors.
Last of the Paris visits. Nyack ceases to be his primary residence.
Sells his first canvas, at the Armory Show.
Moves to the apartment at 3 Washington Square North where he will live and work until his death. The inside front cover of Book I gives that address.
« E.H. came in 1913 », in her list of the tenants of number 3 from Glackens on. Her year-by-year chronicle, kept backwards from 1961 to 1906, leaves 1913, 1912 and 1911 blank.
Begins the printmaking that runs into the early 1920s — the etchings that fill the first forty leaves of Book I.
Josephine Verstille Nivison joins the Washington Square Players.
First solo show, at the Whitney Studio Club. He is thirty-seven.
In Gloucester, Massachusetts, meets Josephine Verstille Nivison.
Marries Jo Nivison. From here she keeps the record: “Recorded by Jo N Hopper (Mrs. Edward Hopper) at time each work is finished, or before it leaves studio.”

The Frank K. M. Rehn Galleries begin to represent him, and go on doing so for the rest of his career. “Frank K. M. Rehn” first appears in Book IV in November of this year and then recurs for forty years.
« Gloucester. Honeymoon. Watercolors. Chicago August. » — the first joint year of that chronicle; every year before it is hers alone.
« got car - Dodge », with the summer at Two Lights in the Coast Guard cottage, then Ogunquit and Charleston. Page 116 calls it « the Dodge - 1" car ».
The Whitney Studio Club closes, to make way for the Whitney Museum of American Art.
“Early Sunday Morning” is acquired within months of being finished, and becomes part of the Museum’s founding collection.
First Cape summer: « Cape - Wellfleet then Bird's Cage S. Truro » — the rented Bird's Cage, three summers before they built.
The Whitney Museum of American Art opens, and first acquires his work.
Included in the first Whitney Biennial, and in twenty-nine further Biennials and Annuals down to 1965.
« Cape - last yr. at Bird's Cage. Bgt. land. »
Builds a second home and studio on Cape Cod, and keeps it for the rest of his life. The Truro and South Truro watercolours in Books I and III begin here.
« Cape - Built house. » Her one line for the year, and the whole of it.

« We had covered the ground of all known alternatives on way down — Quebec, Malbai, 2 Lights, Gloucester — none of them pleased — E.H. liked S. Truro better, so that settled. But not the Cobb Cottage again — then our own cottage. » On April 1, « E. made copy of map of S. Truro land. »

Mr. Campbell, « foreman for Truro house », is shown « E.H's Modern Mus. catalogue so he could see the characteristic style of the man whose studio he is building »; by June 20 « the chimney is way up the roof », the west side and the roof shingled, « a very strongly built little house ». Dunlavy is the builder.

« E. working on big new canvas » on December 11, in the notebook PAAM numbers 2389.123 — « Bright Orange Cover, inscribed on first page: Late 1934 1935 ». The one place the typescript names the physical diary it is reading.

« Took House by Evening Park up to Rehn Galleries » on January 9, and « E. got a check for 2 water colors — Coal Box Truro Station — & a little one of Jenners House »; on the 25th, « the news came out E. had been bestowed the Temple Gold Medal for the best picture there at the Philadelphia Academy », Chapin and Moffat on the jury. The typescript carries this January twice, in two typings.

« Returned from the cape, speeded up by telegram that burglars had broken into N.Y. studio » — November 3; Anne's petit-point bag « that E. had designed » among the losses. On December 13 « Dawn Before Gettysburg is on the high seas — off to Italy », bought for Arturo Grossi. Cape Cod Afternoon was painted « all thru Oct. » of this year, the next summer's diary says.

Ernest Brace of Bearsville « came here to interview Eddie for ‘Art’, the Washington magazine » on January 28; the next day « E. has letter from Homer St. Gaudens sais E's coming exhibition is going along smoothly » — the Pittsburgh one-man show, « eight canvases invited are not available » by February 26.

« E. gets telegram from Corcoran in Washington announcing that E. has been given 1st prize and Corcoran gold medal for Cape Cod afternoon » — March 22; on the 26th, at the press view, « had his picture taken with Mrs. Roosevelt by some dozen press photographers in front of his picture ». The six-day bicycle race picture « is finished — needs frame ».

« Letter from Frank R. — to tell that Montclair Mus. has bought Coastguard » (June 15); « Our 13th anniversary » on July 9; in September, « Trip to Vt. Stayed all the time at South Royalton with Mr. & Mrs. Robt. Slater », where « E. got 3 large water colors & 1 small »; in October « Lousy Shacks » begun at the head of the Pamet; « Left Cape — early Nov. »
« Cape Huricane », in her spelling, with a second visit to the Slaters in Vermont. In March, four days of his cold with the temperature taken hour by hour — « E.H. 1938. », pages 107 to 125.

« Va. Mus. jury at Budworth — Eddy, John Carroll, Karfiol, Hopkinson, Daniel Garber » (February 17); « My Eddy off to Richmond » (February 22); and on March 13, « E. not one canvas for nearly a yr — last Ap — did 5 A.M. — no canvas since. »

« Eddy started a little canvas — girl in a pulman. Had me pose for the figure by night light in big pokey hat & hair down. This the first canvas for nearly a year since 5 A.M. (Lighthouse) » — the day before the Architectural League dinner of March 17; « E. showed me his Pulman picture just finished » on the 28th, and it went up to the gallery on the 30th.
« E. wants to change over to Windsor Newton oils — So I'm to inherit gold Rembrandt colors. » May 18 — the change of colourman the Technique tab reads off the ledgers, dated by her to the week.

« Letter from Anne Tucker at Bar Harbor inclosing letter from friend in Paris who had seen the Lighthouse — hung in place of honor at the Jeu de Pommes show » (June 14). July 9: « Anniversary — & E. doing his very best not to start or participate in any fociferous difference ». July 18: « The lease of the Wash. Sq. studio has come — rent raised somewhat », and a beam to be run through the studio.

Boston, August 1 to 4: Dr. Ragle, then « Mass. General ... At Phillips House the desk sent me to 603 » for two days of tests — « Paid bill at Hospital — 95.14 » — and « so many things that E's symptoms might indicate he has not any at all. No anemia ... extra systoles ... not a thyroid case at all »; Benzedrine and vitamin C prescribed. Then « Aug. 19–Sept. 25 — S. Royalton, Vt. E. got 5 or 6 watercolors — 2 others could not be finished because hurricane had changed the landscape. »

« Rehn Gal. to bring up pictures — Frank saw us & we all looked over the season's catch — 8 water colors — 4 large, 4 small (14x20) » (November 25); November 6, « E. answers a very nice letter from Homer St. Gaudens about his picture at the Carnegie International & Early Sun. A.M. borrowed from the Whitney Museum »; December 16, « E. busy making crayon drawings — all dark — of curtained entrance to a box at the theatre »; December 29, « Canvas has acquired 1st rough coat of paint — blocked in. »

« E in studio wrestling with a dark movie interior. It is such a difficult subject. Dusk is always so difficult » (January 1); « Took N.Y. Movie House up to Rehn Gal — where greeted like a new born heir » (February 2), the same day « The City, rescued by auction » from the Duncan Phillips sale « is restored to its original habitat ».

« E home in peace — made 2 fine sketches of new canvas. Bridal path in Central Park with the city outside — riders on the path » (April 2); « He starting a new canvas — praise be ... Every A.M. he goes up to Central Park to get more data » (April 4); « E went out early to look up horses in old magazines. He has a little book of horse anatomy » (April 7); « Men Women & Horses finished, signed & varnished in much hurry to get it up to Rehn Gallery » (April 27).

« Augustus St. Gaudens came to see us ... I'm invited too to the Carnegie International at Pittsburgh — late in Sept. E. & Speicher to 2 Amer. members of the jury » (May 9); « Pittsburgh Expedition. Tues. Sept. 26–Sat. Sept. 30 Carnegie jury of award » — « E had come to vote for [Utrillo] — had had a wretched canvas ».

« [Helen Hayes' House] ... they're so anxious for E to paint it and E. has been trying to side step it, but Frank Rehn so wants E. to do it » (November 3); « He hates the imposed job of painting Helen Hayes' house » (November 8); « E. got canvas stretched ... 40 x 28 or so ... He's taking it from his 2" sketch in crayon » (November 19); « E & I took up to the Rehn Gallery the finished portrait of Pretty Penny » (December 21) — and « E gave me the beautiful drawing of the Helen Hayes house », the drawing the black notebook lists on page 59.

« E. has new picture drawn in charcoal — had 2 highly finished crayon sketches ... It's a business office with older man at his desk & secretary, female fishing in a filing cabinet. I'm to pose for the same to night in a light skirt » (February 1); « We take Office at Night up to Rehn Gallery. It most graciously rec'd. Attempts at christening; John Clancy suggesting: Cordially yours; Room 1566 » (February 22). Frank Rehn phoned that « someone in movie world named Robinson has bought Sunlight on Prospect St. »

« E. wanted to ask whether Frank particularly wanted him to go do jury duty for the Chicago Art Institute next fall. No — said Frank — it would only cut short his summer and fall painting season, that one more canvas would be worth far more ... Chop Suey hangs in the front room — color far richer than when E painted it » (April 25). « E. painting Civil War artillery all day » (April 29); « We took Light Artillery Before Gettysburg up to Rehn Gallery. Frank and John gave it — as usual — the warmest reception » (May 8).

South Truro from June 2; « We got a P.O. box to day — #51 » (June 12); « the loss of that fine old S. Tr. church has denuded the hills » — the church of the etching, burnt; July 18, Boston: « Dr. Ragle ... E. has been better this past winter than he's been in 10 yrs. »; August 12, « E. painted little grey house ... the find he made down Eastham back road. »
« Trip West - Calif., Oregon, Wyoming. »; the forward chronicle of page 44 gives it as « Las Vegas, Los Angeles, Frisco, Portland, O. - Cape », with « Columbia R. » in the margin.

« Summer 1941 — Grand Tour of the West »: May 23, « off, full sail, for California »; St. Louis, where Perry Rathbone « said he was sorry to have no Hopper » and E. told him of « E's 'gas' — filing station with familiar taking of the flying red horse ... E. promptly volunteered: 'It's no good!' »; Kansas City, Wichita (« saw '5 AM' »), Colorado Springs, the Berthoud Pass « in our late Buick, 1935 brand. This 39 is doing it beautifully », Salt Lake, Bryce, the Grand Canyon, Zion, Las Vegas, Boulder Dam, Yuma; « E. did Los Angeles on his own all Tues. When he came back said 'Oh boy, you stay right where you are — Los Ang. is horrible!' »; Walter Arensberg's collection; Santa Barbara, Carmel; Yosemite, « a second honeymoon »; San Francisco and a week at San Mateo, where « E. finished sketch of that fine old house with 2 palm trees »; the redwoods, the Oregon coast, Portland, Yellowstone, Wapiti, Wyoming — « E. began water color at the base of the Holy City rock formations » — the Bad Lands, Cleveland, and Nyack on July 22: « This is the 60" day & the last lap of a gorgeous trip from ocean to ocean and back again ... This is E's birthday ... This A.M. we came to our 10,000 miles. » « E. sais 'curious & wonderful but not moving to him — they have no associations for him.' »

« Peggy Rehn dead » (August 4). September 4: « he gets started on 1st canvas in months ... He hadn't done a canvas since last winter — the burlesque queen — that I posed for before stove. He did 3 good watercolors on the 'grand tour' west »; « tall sailboats one sailing parallel with a grassy hill ... a summer cottage at right side of bluff — got a cupola » (September 5); September 19, Boston, « Dr. R. has put E. on an experiment with pituitary gland ». October 15: « E. went down to Eastham to have another look at house & barn formations he's had an eye on for years & has now started a canvas ... a lot of pavement across front »; October 30: « Yesterday E. finished his picture of the long stretch of handsomely kept up farm house & barn on the road along Eastham way. I'm relieved to have him put in the streak of white — traffic line — across big expanse of grey road. » « E. has 2 fine big ones. »
“Nighthawks”, his most acclaimed composition.

March 17, the Rousseau opening at the Museum of Modern Art: « We met M. Rich of the Chicago Art Inst. there ... He spoke enthusiastically about 'Gas' and I said he must stop in at Rehns to see Nighthawks. » April 20, « E. and I go to funeral of Gertrude Whitney at St. Bartholomew's »; April 21, « E. had changed his canvas — R.R. platform — onto heavier stretchers »; April 28, « E finishes Dawn in Pennsylvania and makes sketch of it in ledger & I write color notes » — the record books being written, in her words.

« Frank Rehn phoned to say the Chicago Art Institute has bought Night Hawks — but is returning a smaller canvas — Girl in Pulman at Night — in partial payment. Not so good to get it back — but fine to have Night Hawks installed in what one hopes a safe place. Frank told E. that he had shown Alfred Barr of the Modern Art Mus. E's latest — Dawn in Pa. — empty R.R. Station & Barr had said he thinks E.H. — the most exciting painter in America » (May 11); « got fat check for Night Hawks. Girl in Pulman returned from Art Inst. in a new frame, most unbecoming » (May 13); « E. collected 2nd load of early canvases left from show of early work, Jan. 41 » (May 28).

At South Truro from June 10, and « This is an entirely wasted summer for painting ... E. began a second water color down near Cobb house but paper gets too soaked to work. He can't afford to use tires to go hunting down in his own particular happy hunting ground at Eastham » (September 17); « E isn't getting any pictures this summer with the worst painting weather until just now & gasoline rationing & need to skimp on use of tires » (October 13). « In same mail check from Frank for Dawn in Penn. » (July 18).
First Mexico: « Mexico - City, Saltillo, Sept. Monterrey », « by R.R.! », « no Cape ». Page 48 lists every Mexican journey to 1957 under the heading « To get this straight ».
The whole of the year in the typescript is one sheet of three lines: « Mar. — Trip to Washington — Corcoran Gallery / 1943 Mexico — late June — Oct. 1" / 1944 — South Truro. »

« E. has begun a new canvas: here and row of trees of right, broad road on left » — September 25, at South Truro; « E got a fine start with his canvas » on October 1. Page 325 opens with the same four lines of chronicle the black notebook carries on its page 21.

« June 21, '44 Wed. Left N.Y.C. » with a night at the du Bois's in Stonington; June 22, South Truro: no water, « word had gone forth by underground last year that those Hoppers had gone to Mexico, so a gang of mice had moved in »; « we are indeed fortunate to find so little the matter with everything when we'd been gone nearly 2 years ». July: the car's engine out in Boston, and Dr. Butterfield at the Cape Cod Hospital for E.

« E. stretches canvas for sketch he has concocted. Praise be — it's a sail boat. It's been so hard for E. to get started this year — the house, the car, his health » (August 10); « Martha, Reggie & E. sailed in little borrowed boat » (August 12); « He is now answering Rolland McKinney's request for drawings for exhibit at Mus. of Hist. Science and Art in Los Angeles » (August 23); « Paris has been retaken! » by the Lombard radio (August 25); « I go out on R.R. wharf to look at guls ... so that E. could get good look at guls for his present canvas » (September 2); « The canvas is getting along fine — it's an all blue picture sea & sky — It might be E. himself at the rigger »; « He sais he isn't painting fact in this picture — but thought » (September 8).

« Fri. Sept. 15". The Hurricane of 1944 » — « we have known high winds here in the fall & we fell asleep. It was after 1 I awoke — such a din of wind & deluge — it felt as though the house was down on the beach instead of 60 ft. above »; « The little house stands firm, except that windows may have been sand scratched — not a thing the matter. » « E. has one canvas the sail boat with bar guls — which he doesn't like ... this the 15" year » (September 14); « summer is gone, no pictures » (September 18).
« Xmas 44 E. elected to Instit. of Arts + Letters »; « Cape - ap. Salmagundi Prize ».
« Mexico - Sattillo Grand Titon Cape. », with « Buick 39 » in the margin — the second Mexico, by car.

April 22, the Century Club's Henri show « & 5 of his: Bellows, Kent, du Bois, Speicher, Hopper »; April 26, « He has big dinner at Arts & Letters to-night »; and Josephine Hopper's « own homemade one man show » on Washington Square North, which WQXR announced on the air.

« We finally set forth for Mexico » — May 7; San Antonio and Laredo on the 15th, « climbing one of the Sierra Madres on the way to Monterrey » on the 16th, then Saltillo, where « E. — a watercolor of housetops » and « E. says he feels like a prisoner here — waiting for a sky ». July 2, « Left Sortillo — in Texas three days, corner of N. Mexico, and Colorado »; « Wyoming 10 days », where « E. gets a fine watercolor of Mt. Morain »; through Yellowstone and Shoshone Canyon; « Back to N.Y. City Sat. July 27 ».

On the Cape: « This is our 17th year — 16th not counting 1943 in Mexico all summer — so he's about covered all that interests him. » On September 29 « E working on first oil since last spring. A gloomy looking house & fields », and Josephine Hopper signs a contract with Samuel Golden for a reproduction of her Oil Lamp.
« # 3 invasion by N.Y.U. » — the whole of the year's line, and the beginning of the Washington Square fight that fills two of the other notebooks.
« Group of 6 or 7 paintings at Rehn. very successful. » Then, in February, « N.Y. Hospital - Prostate », the Grosvenor Hotel after it, « Stayed into May », and « 3 trips to N.Y. Hos. hemmorhages ».

« E's show in Jan. — was going over so big — such fine press, so many reproductions & people applauding » — the Rehn show that « started 1st Mon. in Jan. 48 — & kept up until Nov. 7th or 8th & next day E. off to the N.Y. Hospital ». By August, « There hasn't been one picture since the fall of 1947. »

« I worked on his ledger, went thru old catalogues to see that any reproduction of his work should be listed in ‘Reproductions and Reviews.’ The ledger — or those ledgers have grown out of rudimentary affairs before success & publicity » — June 24: the record books, in her words, as she kept them. The same week « Duncan Phillips has sent check for ‘Approach to a City’ ».

« E. having been chosen as the painter of 1950 to be featured with an entirely too inclusively one man show » — the Whitney retrospective, two years ahead; « Miss Irven bragged that she had all the data from my ledger, so they can go right ahead & put their figures on everything ». Rosalind Irvine of the Whitney stands on the black notebook's page 35.

« Telegram comes from Alfred Frankfurter, Arts News, to inquire about date Compartment C was painted. E. does know — can't remember »; she wires back « that Compartment C had been painted about 10 yrs. ago & that the ledger was not here to make exact date » — August 26 and 27, at Truro, the ledgers in New York.

« E. drawing in charcoal on a 30 x 40 canvas. It turns out to be a shop window with trees at left [7 A.M.] — & a clock in window » — September 7; « about finished his first canvas since last fall » on the 22nd, « done this canvas in 16 days », stretched on Labor Day. The Babcock Galleries send $20 for an etching of Night Shadows.

« E. took new canvas — 7 A.M. up to Rehn Gallery; heard of sale of Office at Night to Minneapolis Mus. » — November 6; on the 10th, the Whitney opening, « E had his Night Hawks there », borrowed back from the Art Institute of Chicago, « to have its old frame back on ».
The Whitney organises his second career retrospective. Leaf 2 of Book I is headed with a note of it.

« Retrospective Ex. Hopper, Man of the Year at Whitney Mus. - W. 8" St. E. in hospital at opening of Exhib. » The show goes on to Boston and Detroit, and in Chicago « E. degree D.F.A. » at the Art Institute, « stayed at Palmer House. + parties ».

« Left Washington Square » July 18 for Truro; August 18, « the corner of Route 6 & the Main St. of Orleans in down on canvas in blue paint »; August 31, « paper model for High Noon » on the desk; October 12, « E. has about finished his Bay Window picture & is well pleased with it. Says better than High Noon. » November 4, « Note from Met to tell E. his Conference at Night has passed both juries ».

« Mexico - Sattillo in heat wave. On to Santa Fé + return to Cape - began efforts for Electric. » The backwards chronicle puts the Chicago degree here: « E. gets degree Dr. of Fine Arts - Chicago Art Inst. »
« Mexico — Lv. N.Y. May 28, '51 », in the heading of the summer's diary; then « July 22 (in Nyack) », « Tues. 24 (in N.Y.) », « Thurs. July 26 off early to Cape ».

« Dec. 7 or 6 off for Mexico - via El Paso, TX. + South. Stay at Guanacinato (Posada de la Presa », in her spelling — after « Water Color Show at Metrop. » and, in September, « By air to N.Y. for Metrop. jury ».

« from Guanajuato - middle of Jan on to Mitla, Oaxaca », « Feb. on to Puebla », Monterrey, and « back to N.Y. Mar. 1" in time for jury duty at Virginia Mus. at Richmond »; « Whitney Annual Oct. 53 Fire Escape ».
« S. Truro. E. N.Y. Hos. hernias - Feb. »; Gloucester in September « trees », and Frank Rehn.

« for this he gets the Arts & Letters largest award » — the gold medal, and Time's « Gold for Gold » article of May; the one canvas of the summer, « South Carolina », whose « oil hasn't dried yet so he couldn't send it to the Whitney opening »; the Arts and Letters dinner at the Knickerbocker Club on November 14.
« Dec. 6" 1956 H. H. + Pacific Palisades » until June 6, 1957 — page 47 gives the address as « H. H. F. Pacific Palisades, Calif. », and the initials are not expanded here.

« E. surely much hunted this summer of 1956. Time Mag. doing his head on its cover & a sizeable article. Art News to do long article for their Annual of 1956, the Worcester Telegram Gazette Sun. Mag. doing illustrated article by Frank Crotty. The Huntington Hartford award as their reason for highlighting him — all 3 at once » — August 7; forty photographs by Mr. Vandervert on the 9th; Time's researcher met « at new Texaco Service Station, Truro » on the 23rd; « a fat check for E. had arrived — the award from the Harrington Hartford Foundation » on September 18.

« E painting all day. Old man sitting outside gas station » — September 26; « The white wall of the gas station will recall the white wall of office in Small City » (October 8); « E. finishing his latest canvas: cold & clear » (October 11). « Late Oct. 1956: He did only that one big oil & an unfinished watercolor of mt. tops — no sky. »
« N.Y. Hos. Jan. 29, 58 », then « burglar Feb. 11", 58 » — the burglary page 3 may allude to in « from trunk in basement (burglars) ».
« Moved to Greenwich Gallery - 71 Washington Place - Mar. 1958 » — her dealer, not his. The notebook lists her group show there, the four hundred announcements she sent, and who came.
« T.V. performance at Boston Mus. Ap. 10, 1961 », « E. H. + J. H. », at the Sheraton Plaza; « Tape recorded in N.Y.C. - Sat. Ap. 29, 61 » with Brian O'Doherty.
A second Whitney retrospective in his lifetime, organised by Lloyd Goodrich — a lifelong friend, and the donor of four of these six ledgers.
Last of the Whitney Biennials and Annuals he takes part in.
Dies in the studio at 3 Washington Square North. Book IV’s final entry is dated 23 March.
Jo Hopper dies ten months after Edward, having been hospitalised. Their artistic holdings — nearly three thousand items — are bequeathed to the Whitney.
The Whitney publishes the catalogue raisonné, twenty years in the making. It was made from these books.

disputed.about: When he took the top floor of 3 Washington Square North
disputed.what: The Whitney's artist page says he lived and worked in the same Washington Square apartment from 1913 until his death; other chronologies give 1929 for a move to the top floor of the building. Both may describe the same tenancy at different scales. Only the Whitney's wording is used above, because mixing two sources into one sentence is how a date nobody stated gets published. Her black notebook adds a third voice: the list of the tenants of the house on page 117 says « E.H. came in 1913 », while her own year chronicle leaves 1913 blank.

disputed.about: When Chicago gave him the degree
disputed.what: The black notebook says it twice. Page 45's forward chronicle puts « Chicago Art Institute - E. degree D.F.A. » after the Detroit leg of the 1950 retrospective; page 20's backwards chronicle lists « E. gets degree Dr. of Fine Arts - Chicago Art Inst. » under 1951. Both are hers, and both stand above under their own year.

Page 19 of the black notebook has « Boston Mus. T.V. Ap. 20 (N.Y. Mar. 29) »; page 61 has « Ap. 10, 1961 », the stay at the Sheraton Plaza « Sat. Ap. 8 - Mon. Ap 10" », and the tape « recorded in N.Y.C. - Sat. Ap. 29, 61 ». The fuller page is the one quoted above; the other is not corrected.

disputed.about: Which Christmas the Institute elected him
disputed.what: The black notebook's page 21 writes under 1945: « Xmas 44 — E. elected to Instit. of Arts + Letters ». Page 325 of the PAAM typescript, Part V, carries the same four lines of chronicle and writes « xmas '45 few days before E.H. elected to Amer. Institute of Arts and letters ». One is a copy of the other, and the pages do not say which; both stand.

disputed.about: How many times the studio was burgled
disputed.what: Three, if the two sources are read together, and neither says so. The typescript's Part I has the telegram of November 1936; its Part V has « fall of 1947 trunks in cellar pried open with an ax, most everything else toted off by vandals »; the black notebook has « burglar Feb. 11", 58 » on page 19 and, on page 3, frames put on a shelf « Nov. 1948 — from trunk in basement (burglars) », where the word is doubtful. The 1948 frames and the 1947 trunks may be one event.

disputed.about: A diary typed twice under two years
disputed.what: Pages 219 to 235 of Part IV are headed « 1942 II Summer — S. Truro », and every entry on them — the trip west, Peggy Rehn's death, the sailboat canvas of September — is the 1941 diary that Part III already carries on pages 191 to 204 under its own year. The typescript's heading is a slip; nothing from those pages is booked under 1942 here.

disputed.about: Which day the Institute dinner fell on in 1955
disputed.what: Part V's page 360 has the Institute of Arts and Letters dinner at the Knickerbocker Club « on Nov. 15 » in 1950; its page 366 has one on « Mon. 14 Nov. » in 1955. Two dinners five years apart, or one misremembered: the typescript does not say, and both stand.
